title: Glasgow's Green Gates Named Fourth-Best Casual Dining Spot in UK
excerpt: TripAdvisor's 2026 Travellers' Choice Awards placed the Merchant City Indian tapas restaurant fourth nationally for casual dining — ahead of anything in London — on the strength of its viral naan bowls and shareable plates.
body:
• Green Gates Indian Restaurant in Glasgow has been ranked the fourth-best casual dining restaurant in the UK in TripAdvisor's 2026 Travellers' Choice Awards, ahead of every venue in London.
  • The Merchant City restaurant's Indian tapas — curries served in edible naan bowls that have gone viral online — and a value-for-money pre-theatre menu won over reviewers. It also placed sixth in the world for vegan & vegetarian restaurants.
  • Two branches to visit: 24 Candleriggs in Merchant City and Sauchiehall Street. TripAdvisor's Best of the Best awards draw on a year of traveller reviews and ratings, placing winners in the top 1% of listings.
  • Glasgow doubled up: Momo Hub Mother Nepal also cracked the UK top ten, landing at number nine.

The news

Glasgow has a new national food trophy to celebrate. Green Gates Indian Restaurant has been named the fourth-best casual dining restaurant in the United Kingdom in TripAdvisor's 2026 Travellers' Choice Awards, outranking every restaurant in London — a city that usually dominates national dining lists.

The UK casual-dining top five reads: Casa Brazilian Rodizio in York first, Makars Gourmet Mash Bar in Edinburgh second, Lavang Shirley in Solihull third, Green Gates Merchant City fourth, and Vincenzo Trattoria in Manchester fifth. London's first entry, Andy's Greek Taverna, appears only at number six. A second Glasgow venue, Momo Hub Mother Nepal, placed ninth.

Context & background

Green Gates runs two branches — 24 Candleriggs in Merchant City and a second on Sauchiehall Street — and has served Scotland's Indian-food lovers for more than 15 years, specialising in home-style regional cooking from the north and south of India. Its signature is Indian tapas: small, shareable plates of classics, headlined by the naan bowl — a curry served in a bowl made of naan bread — which has become one of the restaurant's most photographed dishes.

TripAdvisor's Travellers' Choice Best of the Best awards are decided on the quality and quantity of traveller reviews and ratings posted over a 12-month period, backed by an editorial review process. Winners sit among the top 1% of listings on the platform, so a fourth-place finish reflects sustained reviewer enthusiasm rather than a single viral moment.

"Their must-try tapas-style Indian dishes are perfect for sharing, and the attentive service and generous portions make it a great spot for groups. Don't miss the pre-theatre menu for good value."

— TripAdvisor, Travellers' Choice Awards 2026

Impact & analysis

The result is a genuine feather in the cap for Glasgow's food scene. Scotland's biggest city has a deep, long-standing love affair with Indian food — its curry houses are institutions — but national awards lists are usually weighted toward London and the southeast. Taking fourth in the country, with a second Glasgow Indian venue in the top ten and a sixth-place world ranking for vegan and vegetarian food, signals how far the city's dining reputation has travelled.

The format matters too. Tapas-style Indian dining — smaller plates, shared across the table — has been one of the most successful reinventions of the traditional curry house, and Green Gates is a case study in doing it well: relaxed setting, generous portions, and a pre-theatre menu that keeps prices approachable.

Diaspora angle

For the Indian diaspora, the win is familiar in the best way. Indian restaurants are woven into Britain's high streets, and awards like these reward the diaspora-run businesses that keep that tradition alive while evolving it. Green Gates' home-style regional cooking — northern and southern Indian dishes under one roof — mirrors what many second- and third-generation families actually eat, and the tapas format suits exactly how those families order: a little of everything, shared.

What's next

The 2026 Travellers' Choice results are final, so the next national reckoning comes with the 2027 awards. Reviewers keep reviewing, and rankings shift year to year — but for now, Green Gates has the kind of national recognition that tends to bring queues. Booking ahead at either Glasgow branch is the practical move.
